nodes.procedure: The Ni sheet was first cleaned by ultrasonic in 20 vol% HCl for 30 min, then rinsed by deionized water to remove surface oxides and pollution then dry in room temperature.

nodes.name: Ni-Cu-P electrodeposition (NCP-0)
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition using IT6874A DC power supply with carbon rod as anode and cleaned nickel sheet as cathode. The electrodeposition electrolyte was prepared with 0.2 M NiCl2·6H2O solution, 0.2 M NaH2PO4·H2O solution, 0.25 M NH4Cl solution and 0 M CuCl2·2H2O solution. Constant current density at 10 mA cm⁻² continued 20 min. The as-prepared sample was dried in a vacuum oven directly.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Cu-P catalysts on Ni sheet show Ni peaks at 44.5°, 51.9°, 76.4°; Cu peaks at 43.36°, 50.56° in NCP-3, NCP-4; NCP-2 powder XRD shows Cu97P3 (JCPDS 65-9049) phase with minor NiP2 at 36.5°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S9a shows the XRD patterns of Ni-Cu-P catalysts deposited on Ni sheet, the three high intensity peaks at 2θ = 44.5°, 51.9° and 76.4° correspond to Ni sheet feature characteristic peaks. Cu feature characteristic peaks at 2θ = 43.36° and 50.56° can be detected in NCP-3 and NCP-4. ... It can be seen that the Cu97P3 (JCPDS 65-9049) can be obtained. The small amount of NiP2 (2θ = 36.5°) can be also detected in the NCP-2.

nodes.characterization_summary: NCP-2 exhibits pine-needle like nanotubes stacked disorderedly among cracks; NCP-3 shows pine-needle like dendrite with closer, finer, narrower tubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CNP-2 (Fig. 2c, d) surface turns loose and porous, the pine-needle like nanotubes can be well formed at the certain Cu contents, and stacked disorderedly among the cracks of Ni-Cu-P films. The CNP-3 (Fig. 2e, f) also shows a pine-needle like dendrite structure, the branches stick closer, the tubes become very fine and narrow.

nodes.characterization_summary: NCP-2 pine-needle like nanotubes have uniform branch tube thickness ~19 nm, internal diameter 24 nm; SAED shows discrete spots indexed to fcc Ni (JCPDS 04-0850).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures 3 shows the pine-needle like nanotube structures of NCP-2, the average thickness and internal diameter of the branch tube is uniform ∼19 nm and 24 nm respectively... The SAED (Figure 3b corresponding to Figure 3a) constitute by discrete spots, which can be indexed to face-centered Ni (JCPDS 04-0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: NCP-3 shows similar pine-needle structure but with thicker ~43 nm nanotube walls, few remaining nanotube branches, other branches rod-shaped; SAED indexes to Ni lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures S10a and b show that the similar pine-needle like structure could be also obtained in the NCP-3 catalysts. However, Figure S10c demonstrates that there are only a little nanotube branches remain, the wall of nanotube become much thicker ∼43 nm. Other branches will change to rod-shape structure. The inset SAED patterns index to the Ni lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: NCP-2 survey confirms Ni, Cu, P; Ni 2p: Niδ+ 853.0 eV (phosphides), Ni2+ 856.2/858.1/873.8/875.3 eV (phosphates); Cu 2p: Cuδ+ 932.8 eV (phosphides), Cu2+ 934.6/935.7/952.6/954.9 eV (phosphates); P 2p: 133.1 eV (POx).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p (Figure 4b) spectrum, the binding energy at 853.0 eV belong to Niδ+ in metal phosphides. ... The Cu 2p XPS spectrum (Figure 4c) also shows the Cuδ+ in metal phosphides with the binding energy of 932.8 eV. ... For the P 2p spectrum shown in Figure 4d, the peak at 133.1 can be assigned to the oxidized POx.

nodes.characterization_summary: NCP-0 EDS reveals homogeneous Ni and P distribution on deposited film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS testing and element mapping (Figures S3, S4) reveal nickel element and phosphorus element distributed on the deposited film homogeneously.
